thread:
maya: Heads-up — small/large request mix is stomping micro-windows and triggering expensive evictions. Thinking about two approaches: coordinated drain windows on enqueue vs improving soft-evict heuristic. Anyone seen a clear perf/cost win for mixed workloads?

lee: +1 investigate. Soft-evict is simpler but tends to harm tiny, latency-sensitive reqs when a large request arrives.

anil: Sketch the coordinated drain idea? Per-tenant or per-batcher?

maya: Start per-batcher. On enqueue we can mark small reqs and reserve a tiny drain window (4-16ms) so a microbatch can finish without being preempted by a large request. If a large arrives it either waits or routes to another lane. Goal: improve p99 for tiny reqs.

rachel: Feels like lane separation. Main worry: fragmentation of GPU slots and utilization hit during low QPS.

tim: Headroom blow-up is real. Reserve too much and batching efficiency suffers — cost up. Need metrics: eviction rate, wasted tokens, p99 small.

maya: Hybrid proposal: enable coordinated drains only when small_req_ratio > X, otherwise keep soft-evict. That limits fragmentation.

lee: My hypothesis: coordinated drains cut small-req p99 by ~30-50ms but cost ~3-8% throughput loss in bursts. Worth a canary.

anil: Implementation complexity: requires cheap enqueue admission token or cross-batcher signaling. Also define "small" (token_count < 64?).

maya: Tokens < 64 as a heuristic. Quick config sketch below:

```yaml
batcher:
  coordinated_drain:
    enabled: auto
    drain_window_ms: 8
    small_token_cutoff: 64
    min_utilization_pct: 70
  soft_evict:
    threshold: 0.75
    backoff_ms: 12
```

rachel: Expose telemetry: small_req_ratio, eviction_count, lost_tokens_due_to_reservation, kv_warmup_delta. Canary must track cost delta per-GPU-hour.

tim: Add a circuit-breaker: if reservation causes queue build-up > 50ms fall back to soft-evict to avoid cascades.

lee: Routing to a different lane needs pre-warmed tiny-lane or separate pool. Cold starts for tiny-lane are bad; prefer intra-GPU scheduling unless unavoidable.

anil: For prototype do local enqueue-marking only (no cross-batcher signals). On enqueue mark item "drain_protected" if small and recent p99 regressions. Batcher honors that flag for next N ms. Simple rollout.

maya: Action items: 1) lee to implement enqueue-mark + drain-window prototype (owner: lee). 2) rachel to add telemetry panels (small_req_ratio, protected_evictions, p99_small_req, gpu_util). 3) tim to add circuit-breaker fallback if queueing > 50ms.

lee: I'll push a feature-flagged prototype and run a canary across three low-traffic hosts.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for feature batcher.coordinated_drain=on (canary-3 hosts).

rachel: For evaluation capture p50/p95/p99 for small and large, eviction_rate, token_throughput, GPU_util, and cost-per-1k-requests. Also kv-cache warmup impact.

tim: Note: kv-cache/quant warmup might interact badly—tiny-drain could preempt a request that benefits from warmed KV and regress TPU/GPU token cost. Add to telemetry.

anil: If prototype looks promising, long-term we should consider adaptive drain sizing instead of static ms (feedback loop from observed latency).

maya: Agreed. Keep first iteration minimal risk. Thanks all :thumbsup:
